newsitem.title: USA: Tobacco plaintiff's lawyer wins paper's award.
newsitem.headline: Tobacco plaintiff's lawyer wins paper's award.

text.p: The plaintiff's lawyer who won a jury verdict in August against Brown & Williamson Tobacco Co. has been named one of eight "Lawyers of the Year" by Lawyers Weekly USA, the publication said Tuesday.

Norwood "Woody" Wilner of Jacksonville, Fla., who won the second award in history against a tobacco company, was among those cited for having a profound effect on their community, the law or society, said Susan Hall, publisher of the Boston-based national newspaper.
"We chose these eight extraordinary lawyers not for the causes they represent, but because they proved that single lawyers are affecting the world we live in," she said in a statement.

Wilner, who rides a pink bicycle with a big basket full of files to his small firm in Jacksonville, Fla., won the $750,000 verdict against Brown & Williamson. The verdict raised fears that the public attitude had turned against tobacco companies and sent industry stocks plummeting.
Others named by the paper were:
-- Willie Gary of Stuart, Fla. who won a 1996 verdict awarding a funeral home $500 million over a contract dispute in the largest verdict in Mississippi history.
-- Lise Iwon of Wakefield, R.I., who volunteers her time helping women and children who are victims of domestic abuse.
-- Davis Carr, a defence attorney in Mobile, Ala., who has fought for tort reform in his state, where punitive damage awards have increased 600 percent in the last six years.
-- Mario Mandina of Kansas City, Mo., who helped created the National Lawyers Association.

-- John Edwards and David Kirby of Raleigh, N.C., who use "nice guy" professionalism and "tenacious lawyering" in and out of the courtroom to prevent negotiation deadlocks and drawn out trials, while working to better their clients' lives.

-- Richard Seaton of Manhattan, Kan., who won a First Amendment case before the U.S. Supreme Court on behalf of an independent contractor seeking the right to speak out against local governments and public boards.
